### Team 3795 — retained-ledger route preview reserved

New additive consumer scope in [multi-agent-fanout-engine](https://github.com/Jacob-Met/multi-agent-fanout-engine), exact current main `9fe49691944cacf666e1c37f526c0d26fc1a4ee1`, tree `f25d46b79a87c6c88bbbfe5bbae9ced9cb34f020`. Repository Issues are disabled, so this is the shared coordination record. Bounded intake read the 21-open-PR inventory, targeted all-state route/ledger searches and relevant ownership comments; no matching retained-route preview reservation appeared. PR59 blockers, PR68 HTML/native receiving, PR54 identity and all dispatch/export/worker-admission scopes retain their existing owners.

The existing authored-plan preview correctly describes initial readiness. A retained-handoff operator also needs the routes for work that is queued and dependency-ready in the current saved ledger. This is an additive missing consumer, not a defect claim. Exact source fence: new `fanout_engine/queued_routes.py`, `tests/test_queued_routes.py`, `docs/queued-routes.md`, and an append-only README link. No existing ledger, inspection, routing, dispatch, Hub, plan, example, package or workflow edit.

Public CLI: `python -B -m fanout_engine.queued_routes --database EXISTING --project EXACT_ID --routes ROUTING.json`. These three required options occur once; abbreviations/unknown/duplicate options refuse before file access. Help is read-only. Output is stdout JSON only; no output-file option. Existing regular routing admission is reused (256 KiB, catalog/pool each at most 256), with the same strict JSON and authorized model/effort semantics. This consumer accepts at most 256 retained parts and a 4 MiB encoded report. All explicit override IDs must belong to the retained plan, and all overrides must be authorized even if their parts are not currently ready. This stricter whole-configuration preview validation does not alter dispatch's selected-only timing.

One `inspect_project` call supplies the complete validated SQL snapshot. Output keys: `schema_version:1`, `project_id`, `plan_digest`, `state_counts`, `queued_ready_ids`, `blocked_queued_ids`, `parts` (each exact `id`, `state`, `unmet_dependencies`), `routes` (each `part_id`, `route:{model,effort}`, `route_source:explicit|pool`, stored `idempotency_key`), `configured_step_up` (route object or null), and `routing_input_sha256` for the exact routing file bytes. Parts and selected routes preserve retained plan order. Only queued parts whose direct prerequisites are completed receive selected routes. In-flight, unknown, failed and completed states remain explicit context. Configured step-up is metadata only.

Exit 0 means a complete advisory report, including an empty route list; 3 means unknown project; 2 means usage, input/admission, malformed record or read failure; 1 means stdout failure. Complete validation/encoding precedes success output (a broken stream can still receive a prefix). The database is opened through `Ledger.open_readonly`: no SQL writes, schema creation, reservation, worker availability check, dispatch, reconciliation, retry or external action. Ordinary SQLite locking/WAL behavior still applies; this is not a globally immutable filesystem claim. Stored instructions/evidence/artifact locators are not emitted or followed by this projection.

Worker two owns independent original-first expectation/actual CLI receiving; worker three owns source/contract review. Only owned fictional local fixtures will execute. No native service or installed state mutation, Actions creation/dispatch or scheduled continuation. [skip ci] [skip actions]
